A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Committed Q-learning research. All 18 pages, including figures, equations, and Appendices A–E, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 3 and Figure 3 report original simulations comparing Committed Q-learning with regular Q-learning across six corridor lengths.

after.justification: v2 retains the original corridor simulations and their learning curves, reported over 1,000 random seeds in Figure 3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same Q-learning update, option sampling, and commitment until the observed feature changes. The mathematical clarifications do not alter the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same corridor task with lengths 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, and 200. The T-maze remains a theoretical illustration rather than an additional evaluated task.

E2.justification: Figure 3 compares the same methods: Committed Q-learning and regular, non-committed Q-learning. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The numerical example retains the same exploration and step-size schedules, interaction range, and greedy-policy optimality metric. The changed reward in Section 4 belongs to a mathematical example, not the reported experiment.

E4.justification: The corridor-length comparison is unchanged, and neither version adds further empirical ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses. Corrections to theoretical examples are assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Both Figure 3 captions specify 1,000 different random seeds and 95% bootstrap confidence intervals. No statistical reporting procedure changes.

E6.justification: Figure 3's curves and uncertainty bands are identical. Both versions report convergence toward the optimal policy for Committed Q-learning and failure of regular Q-learning; no experimental result entries change.

T1.justification: Section 4 changes the illustrative left-terminal reward from 2 to 1, and Lemma B.6 corrects the up-action probability from 1−δ to δ. Reachability is consolidated in Section 2, with corresponding domain revisions in Appendix C; Appendix D explicitly specifies an infinite horizon. The main theorem and proof strategy remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and convergence claim under rewire-robustness. Explicit reactive-policy wording in Theorem 3.5 and Lemma 4.4 clarifies the scope already stated in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly states an infinite-horizon qualification for its learnability argument; v1 mentioned stationary-distribution convergence without that explicit qualification. Other mechanism explanations and the limitations discussed in Section 7 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed experimental schedules and code-access information are unchanged. No implementation, hardware, runtime, or additional reproduction instructions are introduced.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds explicit citations to Tsitsiklis (1994) and Borkar and Meyn (2000) for standard Q-learning convergence analyses. Both works were already cited elsewhere; the bibliography's membership and substantive research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits clarify reactive optimality, replace several uses of stationary distribution with on-policy distribution, and make policy dependence explicit in expectations. Reachability explanations are consolidated, while the section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Theorem 3.5's implication diagram receives a longer reactive-policy label, Figures 2 and 4 have small caption edits, and text and equations reflow locally. All six numbered figures remain, with unchanged diagrams and experimental curves.

improvement.justification: The corrected reward in Section 4 makes the stated greedy-policy thresholds consistent, and Lemma B.6 now uses complementary action probabilities matching Figure 6. These corrections and clearer theoretical qualifications improve precision, while the central contributions, algorithm, and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
